title: Decompose auth dependency surface and stage JOSE + SAML library upgrades
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Refactor the platform auth surface to isolate JWT/JOSE parsing, TLS/OpenSSL bindings, and SAML adapters so we can perform safe, staged upgrades of jose/jwt, oauth libraries, and OpenSSL-compatible components with minimal runtime risk. This ticket includes creating shims, an integration test matrix, and a gradual rollout plan across hosted and dedicated runtimes.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a clear lib boundary: auth/jose, auth/tls, auth/saml modules with documented public interfaces
Create compatibility shims that allow side-by-side deployment of new JOSE library without changing callers
Upgrade JOSE (jose-lib) to v4.x in staging and pass end-to-end JWT + session flow tests for both RS256 and ES256 keys
Replace vulnerable OpenSSL transitive dependency in the runtime build pipeline with a vetted, reproducible build (boringssl-compatible) and validate TLS handshake compatibility with our KMS
Add SAML adapter tests exercising common IdP metadata shapes and signature algorithms and upgrade saml-lib to latest stable with regression-free parsing
Provide rollback playbook and automated smoke-checks so we can revert within 10 minutes if token validation errors exceed threshold
Security review completed and sign-off from Security & Platform teams before prod rollout
plan: Phase 1 (Week 1): Audit current dependency graph for all services that perform JWT, OAuth, or SAML operations. Produce matrix mapping service -> dep -> usage surface (sign/verify/parse).
Phase 2 (Week 2): Introduce auth facade packages (auth/jose, auth/tls, auth/saml) with thin adapters for existing libraries. Add unit tests and contract tests for each facade.
Phase 3 (Week 3): Implement JOSE v4 adapter behind a feature flag; deploy to staging. Run integration tests and long-run token regression harness (48h).

Phase 4 (Week 4): Replace OpenSSL transitive build artifacts in runtime image. Coordinate with infra to produce deterministic build and run tls-interop tests with internal clients and KMS-backed signing endpoints.
Phase 5 (Week 5): Upgrade SAML parser package and validate against a corpus of IdP metadata gathered from production integrations. Add additional sanitizers for known xml canonicalization edge cases.

Phase 6 (Week 6): Canary rollout to 5% traffic, monitor token validation error rates, latency p50/p95 for auth paths, and memory/CPU for runtime processes. Escalate if degradation or errors exceed thresholds. Full rollout contingent on canary health.
Phase 7: Post-rollout: Remove legacy adapters and cleanup transitive dependencies; publish migration notes for downstream teams.
rollout_notes: Canary gating: token_validation_errors <= 0.1% and auth latency p95 delta <= +20ms after 30m stable window
If token validation errors spike > 0.5% in canary, automatically rollback to previous release and create hotfix incident
Coordinate dedicated pool deployments with capacity team to avoid simultaneous rebuilds during peak hours
Inform SRE and Support 24h before each canary stage; provide a repro script to simulate token flows
Temporary increased logging for auth.* namespaces will be enabled during canary and automatically downsampled after stable window
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff meeting with Platform, Security, Infra. Agreed scope and initial audit checklist (owner: Carlos).

2025-02-16: Dependency audit complete for 12 services that perform direct JWT validation (list in artifacts). Found three services using deprecated jose v2 and two using vendor-patched saml-lib forks.
2025-02-18: Auth facades scaffolded (auth/jose, auth/tls, auth/saml). Added contract tests and GH action contract check. PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/6821

2025-02-20: Implemented JOSE v4 adapter behind feature flag. Staging deployment succeeded; initial integration tests passed. Observed a small p95 latency increase (+8ms) in token parsing which is within budget.

2025-02-22: Built runtime image without legacy OpenSSL artifact and validated TLS interop against KMS dev endpoints. Found one cert chain edge case; added fallback to alternate trust bundle in adapter.
2025-02-24: Security flagged XML canonicalization vector in one SAML metadata fixture; added sanitizer and submitted PR for saml-lib adapter updates. Security review scheduled 2025-02-26.
notes_for_reviewers: Reviewers should focus on the facade public interfaces and the contract tests — we must avoid API surface changes that ripple into many downstream services.
Pay special attention to the JOSE adapter key handling (ES256 vs RS256) and secure randomness sources for nonce/iv generation.
Check that runtime build changes do not reintroduce symbols that violate our FIPS/backport constraints.
